scope: v64 nominal lifecycle and real sdist-to-wheel tests; no native execution by this reviewer
observations: WeakNominalObservation records weak references to sessions and ctypes buffers only. Constructor/close/entry patches use new=plain wrappers, without MagicMock argument histories. The role stack contains strings, not session objects.

Refusal controls deliberately retain the actual traceback. Reference exceptions are deleted before selected execution. assert_released checks cleared buffer attributes on surviving objects and weakref death of every observed allocation.

The post-type-initialization corruption wrapper calls the real constructor owner entry first, requires a 64-byte frame with action 0, phase 10 and stage 2, changes its magic, and asserts exactly one injection plus an observed type session and no function session.

Partial-allocation controls fail the actual second 65536-byte allocation for constructor or outer, assert that the preceding real 192 MiB or 80 MiB workspace was observed, retain the exact injected MemoryError object and traceback, and require all buffers released.

The installed test creates an actual sdist, verifies every declared resource byte within that archive, builds the wheel from that sdist, installs to an isolated target, then runs Python -I -S with authoring-tools imports and old nominal semantic owners forbidden.

The installed child requires all 11 selected source resources to resolve beneath the installed target and compares the complete Core bytes with the same-native-dependency reference. It also actually executes two stored-loan VM cases.

Fresh subprocess controls cover changed and missing source and image for each of the four new kernels, and changed/missing constructor and outer bundle manifests: 20 refusals total. Each mutation is restored in finally.
No skip decorators or development-only exclusions occur in these two files; selectors come from the shared complete fixture.
limitations: This is independent static source review, not a second native run, RSS measurement or qualification result.

The new tamper matrix explicitly targets the four newly added kernels; the other seven dependency resources are checked as installed and through their existing selection admission. Broader dependency tamper evidence must come from their existing tests.
The review does not assert that the changing global fixture, source inventory or CI/full runner integrations are already frozen or qualified.
